activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem: Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]$, find a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation $Ax=0$ is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution is ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=0,$ where ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

This implies that 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$
